transcript.text:
Try these quick checks:

1. Check if the TV has power
• Is the standby/power light on?
• Press the TV’s physical power button, not only the remote.
• Unplug it for 60 seconds, then plug it back in.

2. See whether there is sound
• Sound but no picture: likely input, HDMI, backlight, or display issue.
• No sound and no picture: could be power, source device, or TV fault.

3. Check the input/source
• Press Input/Source on the remote and select the correct HDMI/input.
• If using a cable box, console, streaming stick, etc., make sure that device is powered on.

4. Check cables
• Reseat the HDMI cable at both ends.
• Try a different HDMI port or cable if available.
• Test another device on the TV, or test the same device on another TV.

5. Open the TV menu
• Press Menu, Settings, or Home.
• If the menu appears, the TV screen is working and the issue is likely the connected device/cable/input.
• If no menu appears, it may be a TV display/backlight problem.

6. Flashlight test
• In a dark room, shine a flashlight closely at the screen while the TV is on.
• If you can faintly see an image, the TV’s backlight has likely failed and needs repair.

If you tell me the TV brand/model and whether you still get sound or a power light, I can narrow it down.

If sound works but the screen is completely black, the most common cause is a failed backlight.

Try this first:

1. Press Home/Menu/Settings
• If you hear the TV respond but see nothing, it points to the TV display/backlight rather than the HDMI device.

2. Do the flashlight test
• Turn the room dark.
• Keep the TV on with sound playing.
• Shine a phone flashlight directly against the screen at an angle, moving it around.
• If you can see a very faint image, menu, or shapes, the LCD panel is still working but the LED backlights have failed.

3. Power reset
• Unplug the TV from the wall for 2 minutes.
• While unplugged, hold the TV’s physical power button for 15–30 seconds.
• Plug it directly into a wall outlet and turn it back on.

4. Rule out an input issue
• Try pressing the TV’s Home/Menu button.
• Try another HDMI input/device.
• If the TV’s own menu is also black, it is not the cable box/console.

If the flashlight test reveals a faint picture, it needs backlight repair—usually replacement LED strips, sometimes a power board. This is repairable, but the screen must be removed, so a shop repair is safer. On smaller/older TVs, repair cost can approach replacement cost.

Avoid repeatedly turning it on and off; if there is a backlight/power-board fault, that can sometimes worsen it.
Tried the torch, I can just see the menu faintly where it shines. No smell or smoke btw.

That confirms the TV’s LCD panel is producing an image, but the LED backlight is not working.

Most likely causes:
• Failed LED backlight strips inside the panel — most common
• Backlight power/LED driver board fault — less common
• Loose internal backlight connection — possible but less likely

No smell or smoke is normal; LED backlights often fail quietly.

What to do:
• Warranty/insurance: Check whether it is still covered. Describe it as “sound works, picture visible only with a torch/flashlight; suspected backlight failure.”
• Repair shop: Ask for a quote for LED backlight strip replacement, including testing the LED driver/power board.
• DIY: Only advisable if you have electronics repair experience. The LCD panel is extremely fragile and must be removed to access the strips. If one strip/LED failed, replacing the full set of strips is generally better than replacing only one LED.
• Replace TV: For a small or older budget TV, replacement may be cheaper than professional repair; for a larger/newer model, backlight repair is often worthwhile.

Until repaired, avoid leaving it powered on for long. The TV is not usually a fire risk simply because a backlight has failed, but unplug it when not in use and stop using it if it begins cycling on/off, gets unusually hot, smells burnt, or makes crackling noises.
